Question: Three runners start running simultaneously from the same point on a \(500\)-meter circular track. They each run clockwise around the course maintaining constant speeds of \(4.4,\) \(4.8,\) and \(5.0\) meters per second. The runners stop once they are all together again somewhere on the circular course. How many seconds do the runners run?
Solution:
For all three runners to meet, the runners traveling at \(5.0\) and \(4.8\) meters per second must meet. Two runners on this track occupy the same point when their traveled distances differ by a whole number of \(500\)-meter laps.

The faster runner gains on the other at \(5.0-4.8=0.2\) meters per second. Their first meeting after the start occurs when that gain reaches one lap, after
\[
\frac{500}{0.2}=2500\text{ seconds}.
\]
Thus all three cannot meet earlier. In \(2500\) seconds, their distances are
\[
4.4(2500)=11000,
\quad 4.8(2500)=12000,
\quad 5.0(2500)=12500
\]
meters. These are respectively \(22\), \(24\), and \(25\) complete laps, so all three are together at the starting point. They run for \(\boxed{2500}\) seconds, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
